jane_customer: hitting 401 + very slow responses on /v1/generate this morning. Got a request_id from our client: req_9f3b7a12. Happened around 2024-02-19T10:12Z. Attached a minimal curl we used — can someone check server logs?

sara_support: sorry about that — we can dig. Do you have the exact request_id header value (X-Request-Id or request_id in body) and the full curl? Also, were you using an API key from the prod project or a service token?

jane_customer: here's the curl we ran (sanitized keys):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-alpha","prompt":"hello","request_id":"req_9f3b7a12"}'
```
Headers in response: HTTP/2 401, x-server-request: xsr-78b1, x-latency-ms: 1834.

sara_support: thanks. I tried a quick search but not seeing that request_id in the hot index range. Jamal, can you run a KQL search across recent indices? Might be in archived shards or sampled traces.

jamal_logs: running search now. Quick KQL I used: 
```kql
index: redwood-logs-* AND (request_id.keyword: "req_9f3b7a12" OR headers.X-Request-Id.keyword: "req_9f3b7a12")
```
Also tried a time-bounded query: `@timestamp >= "2024-02-19T10:00:00Z" and @timestamp <= "2024-02-19T10:30:00Z"`

jamal_logs: no hits in hot nodes. Noticed that retention for request-level logs is 14 days for the hot index, then we sample/store traces in long-term archive. If the customer ran this >14d ago we'd need archive job.

michael_oncall: if logs are archived, we can kick off a retrieval but it takes ~24-48h. Before that, can the customer repro quickly and attach the response headers + full verbose curl output? If they can repro we can also ask them to include an extra header so we can correlate edge+app traces: `X-Debug-Session: customer-<id>` and the `X-Request-Id` header.

jane_customer: we can try repro now. What's the exact curl flag to add?

sara_support: add two headers: `-H "X-Request-Id: req_9f3b7a12" -H "X-Debug-Session: support-1708501234"` and run with `-v` so you get response headers. If you can get the full response body + headers paste them here. Also save the terminal output (we can ask engineering for a debug bundle).

jane_customer: ok repro done. Sg, here's the verbose output (trimmed):
```
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/2
> host: api.redwood.ai
> authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> x-request-id: req_9f3b7a12
> x-debug-session: support-1708501234
< HTTP/2 401
< content-type: application/json
< x-server-request: xsr-78b1
< x-latency-ms: 1976
{
  "error": {"message":"invalid api key","code":"auth_invalid"}
}
```

jamal_logs: got it — new copy shows xsr-78b1 which helps. I did a targeted search across the edge index with `xsr-78b1` and found a match: `index: redwood-edge-* AND metadata.server_request_id: "xsr-78b1"`. That led to an edge trace but the downstream app logs were past hot retention.

jamal_logs: KQL for the edge lookup I used: 
```kql
index: redwood-edge-* AND metadata.server_request_id.keyword: "xsr-78b1" | fields @timestamp, metadata.request_id, http.status_code, http.response_time_ms
```

michael_oncall: because the app logs have aged past the 14-day hot retention we have two options: 1) kick archive retrieval (24-48h) which eng-infra handles, or 2) ask customer to re-run with `?debug=true` + `X-Debug-Session` and we can catch a fresh end-to-end trace immediately. Which do you prefer?

sara_support: I'll offer both: ask customer to repro now with debug flag for immediate correlation; if they can't, we'll escalate archive retrieval and keep them updated.

jane_customer: will repro with `?debug=true` now and post results. Thanks — will paste everything here in a few mins. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Automod note — created ticket SUP-2024-0891 to track archive retrieval if needed. Assigned to eng-infra. ETA 48h for archive pull.

sara_support: perfect. Next steps: 1) we wait for repro with `X-Debug-Session` and `X-Request-Id` (immediate correlation possible), 2) if no repro, we proceed with archive retrieval (SUP-2024-0891). I'll update the customer-facing ticket and paste the KQL snippets above for internal runbook.

michael_oncall: FYI for eng-infra: if archive retrieval fails, check trace sampling store and the trace aggregator (trace-store-01) for `metadata.server_request_id: xsr-78b1`. Jamal, can you drop the final KQL into the ticket?

jamal_logs: done — added the two KQL queries and the edge->app correlation steps into SUP-2024-0891.

sara_support: closing loop here; will post an update in ticket once we have repro or archive results. Thanks all.
